title: CLI: supabase link returns password authentication failed for user "postgres"
body: When I run `supabase link --project-ref **********`, or include the database password with `--password`, linking fails with `password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01)`. I copied the project reference from the dashboard's Reference ID. I expect to link my local project to the remote project. I am using macOS Monterey 12.1 and supabase-cli 1.68.6. The project had been paused for a few months and was restored two or three days ago.

symptoms_visible: Running `supabase link` with my project reference fails with `password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01)`.
Passing the database password with `--password` produces the same authentication failure.
N0.label: N0 link authentication failure reported

symptoms_visible: I created a new project for comparison, and `supabase link` fails there too with a failed SASL authentication and `password authentication failed for user "postgres"`.
N1.label: N1 failure reproduced on new project

symptoms_visible: After resetting the database password, `supabase link` still shows the same password authentication error.
N2_x.label: N2_x password-reset aftermath

symptoms_visible: After generating a new access token and logging in with the CLI, I still get the same database authentication error.
N3_x.label: N3_x access-token attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: A project under a new Supabase account still fails to link, although one attempt reports `SASL authentication failed (SQLSTATE 08P01)`.
The same error occurs on a different computer.
With `--debug`, I receive an ErrorResponse whose message is `password authentication failed for user "postgres"` and whose code is `28P01`.
N4_x.label: N4_x account and device replacement aftermath

symptoms_visible: Running the same link command without the environment variable still produces the SASL authentication error.
N_terminal.label: terminal linked using database-password environment variable

question_patterns: Does linking work for any other project, or is it limited to this restored project?
Can you try linking another project and paste the raw result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I only had this project, so I created a new one to test. It fails there too: `failed SASL auth (FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01))`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A newly created project links successfully; only the project that was paused and restored fails.
The new project produces the same authentication failure but without the `Retrying...` line.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c1, reporter RobertB4: in response to the cross-project question, the reporter created a new project and pasted the same raw authentication failure. This is the opening reporter's own account and system chain.

solution.intent: Reset the project's database password in dashboard settings and retry linking.
solution.concrete_example: Reset the database password under the project's Database settings, then rerun `supabase link` with the new password.

edges.comment: Issue c2-c3, reporter RobertB4: the maintainer suggested resetting the database password; the reporter did so and stated that the same error remained.

solution.intent: Generate a new Supabase access token, authenticate the CLI with it, and retry linking.
solution.concrete_example: Create a new access token, log the CLI in with that token, and rerun `supabase link`.

edges.comment: Issue c3, reporter RobertB4: the reporter independently generated a new CLI access token and reported that it did not alter the database authentication failure. This persisted token change is modeled separately from the database-password reset.

solution.intent: Create a new Supabase account and project to avoid a possible account-specific problem, then try linking there.
solution.concrete_example: Create a fresh Supabase account with a new project and test whether `supabase link` works against that project.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c4, reporter RobertB4: the reporter tried their remaining idea of creating a new account and project. They also volunteered that a different computer reproduced the error and pasted their own raw debug ErrorResponse. No later participants' distinct db-push or networking problems are folded into this chain.

solution.intent: Supply the database password through the `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` environment variable for the link invocation, then compare it with a plain invocation to verify that this password-delivery path resolves linking.
solution.concrete_example: Run `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<pass> supabase link --project-ref <ref>`. A shell-handling issue, such as a special character in the password, was suggested as a possibility but was not conclusively established. Confirm that this command prints `Finished supabase link` before treating the issue as resolved.

edges.comment: Issue c7-c8, reporter RobertB4: the CLI maintainer suggested the inline SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD form and only hypothesized that a special character might have interacted badly with bash. The reporter then demonstrated the decisive A/B result: the environment-variable invocation finished linking, while the plain invocation still failed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the established fault boundary: the project reference, account, project, computer, password reset, and CLI access token did not resolve the failure, while supplying the database password through `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` allowed the same link operation to finish.
Must recommend using the database password through `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` for the `supabase link --project-ref <ref>` invocation; a CLI access token is not a substitute for this database credential.

Must not present resetting the database password, regenerating the access token, or replacing the account/project as the resolved fix for this reporter, because each was tried without resolving the authentication failure.
Must not state that special-character handling was conclusively proven as the root mechanism; the thread presents it only as a possible explanation.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the environment-variable invocation finishes linking successfully before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical CLI user who can create projects and accounts, reset credentials, set environment variables, run debug mode, and paste PostgreSQL authentication output.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, persistent, and evidence-oriented; follows suggestions, reports exact command outcomes, and tests hypotheses across projects, accounts, and computers.
